subject: Provider-derived sources for nonauthoritative adopter compatibility
operation_side: existing qualification command and source queries
contract: Resolve the complete ordered required adopter population through the existing authenticated provider identity owner before allocating an exact release runtime, disposable clone, interpreter or evidence train.

Caller roots and interpreters are materialization resources. A root must match the provider-selected repository, exact commit and tree; its branch name or historical green status cannot select the subject.
Reject missing, partial, duplicate, contradictory or unavailable provider identities; no fallback to caller-selected sources or synthetic provider identifiers.

Freeze the complete source inventory during execution. Reauthenticate repository ID, default branch, commit and tree before writing the completed compatibility observation; movement blocks without publishing a partial pass.

Keep authority and publication_authority false, local producer identity and all existing independent provider certification boundaries. This optional compatibility capability cannot make mutable adopter state a publication prerequisite.
Keep ordinary CLI grammar and preserve maintained checkouts; clone and install only within the existing disposable transaction.

Version the source-selection policy as1.4 and document migration from1.3. Continue decoding historical1.3 contracts/receipts for audit, but execution under legacy caller-selected source policy yields a typed migration block before allocation. No implicit policy upgrade or agent-selected source flag.
Keep old receipt schema1.1 as an observation format; exact contract hash distinguishes selection policy. Offline receipt validation alone never authenticates current provider freshness.

Commit contract and failing cause-specific controls before production. Regenerate mirrors only through the canonical owner and qualify source, installed runtime and actual isolated consumers before integration.
positive_tests: Complete provider population resolved in policy order with real numeric IDs and exact branch/commit/tree identities.
Matching clean resource roots are admitted independent of caller argument order; fixed source inventory is unchanged throughout qualification.
The existing full qualification path emits a nonauthoritative result only after provider freshness authentication.
Historical1.3 contract decoding and receipt verification remain available without authorizing new source-selected execution.
negative_controls: Wrong repository, missing/duplicate resources, stale commit or tree reject before runtime or clone allocation.
Provider default branch, repository ID, commit or tree moves after capture; no completed output is written.
Wrong provider reference identity, malformed commit metadata, missing token or partial provider inventory cannot become empty or pinned-local success.
Legacy or contradictory source policy blocks before provider or runtime allocation.
No provider or publisher effect, maintained checkout mutation, arbitrary ref selection or authority escalation.
forbidden_surfaces: Active primary submission bytes or transaction state
Maintained adopter repositories and immutable2.3.4/2.3.5 artifacts
Release collector/publisher applicability or required statuses
Parallel source registry, evaluator, receipt family or fallback source selector
integration: Isolated worktree only while primary3cb3 submission is live. Integrate after its authenticated terminal and scoped qualification; no whole acceptance or phase advancement from this contract.

early_credential_boundary.fact: Credential absence is already known after source policy validation, before hashing assets or reading checkout identities.
early_credential_boundary.requirement: Construct the existing authenticated API client after policy validation and before asset or Git inspection. This is a credential-presence check only; provider GETs still establish actual source identity before allocation.
early_credential_boundary.control: Missing-token consumer path cannot call the asset inventory owner.

installed_consumer_probe.scope: Extend existing fresh/upgrade mixed-toolchain installed-consumer fixture. Bare -I process must prove canonical BCF package absence, import only installed private runtime and exercise provider source capture, numeric identity, freshness rejection and legacy policy block.
installed_consumer_probe.execution: Run only in the next admitted qualification window; no additional heavy train while primary submission is active.
installed_consumer_probe.limits: Fixture-controlled provider GETs prove installed runtime behavior and dependency origin, not real provider or release certification. Existing actual real-provider source query is recorded separately.

contract: GitHub repository names compare case-insensitively for required and frozen inventory uniqueness; duplicate aliases reject before provider reads.
Distinct required repository names must resolve to distinct authenticated numeric repository IDs; no physical adopter can satisfy two required members.
A frozen inventory with repeated numeric IDs or case-equivalent names rejects before collection-time provider reads.
Keep exact policy order, source/freshness checks, existing source identity type and authority false.
Complete synthetic provider full_name metadata for compatibility with the separately qualified shared resolver guard; do not replace real provider checks with test authority.
controls: Duplicate physical repository IDs at capture cannot become a partial or repeated success.
Case-equivalent required repository names reject before any provider request.
Duplicate physical repository IDs and case aliases in frozen inventory reject before collection reads.
